headline: Stocks are set to open sharply higher on the half day, led by chips, after Asia and Europe rallied on Thursday and Friday. A half day on light volume cannot confirm a turn, so Monday is still the first real test.
summary: There was no US session Thursday, so closes here are still Wednesday Nov 25; the dashboard's 'Stale prices' warning is a holiday false alarm, not a missed refresh. At about 9am ET Friday, S&P 500 futures were up 1.7%, Nasdaq 100 futures 2.4% and Dow futures 683 points, with NVDA at 153.19 premarket, up 2.6% (CNBC; MarketWatch). Overseas markets led: the Stoxx 600 rose 1.8% Thursday as the tariff proposals looked less severe than feared, and on Friday the KOSPI rose 4.34%, the Nikkei 2.11% and a Chinese chip index a record 17% (Saxo; CNBC). Early Black Friday reads are solid but partly price: Adobe counted $82.5 billion online Nov 1 to 22, up 9.1%, and Mastercard says about half of its forecast holiday growth is higher prices (FinanceFeeds; mlq.ai). Brent is near $97 on new Iran tension, OPEC meets Sunday, and the Fed's quiet period starts Saturday ahead of the Dec 8 to 9 meeting. Stocks close at 1pm ET today.

regime.why: Unchanged until a follow through day. Friday's half session can rise a lot on light holiday volume, which is why it cannot count. Monday Nov 30 is the earliest full session that could give one. A strong premarket after a 3% intraday drop on Wednesday is a good sign, not proof.

signals.title: The world bought the dip while the US was closed: Europe Thursday, Asia and US futures Friday
signals.what_happened: On Thursday the Stoxx 600 rose 1.8%, the DAX 2.1% and the FTSE 100 1.8%, led by technology, autos and miners, as the proposed US tariffs looked less severe than feared; ASML and Infineon rose more than 3% (Saxo; Minichart). On Friday the KOSPI rose 4.34% to 4,915.68, the Kosdaq 8.13% and the Nikkei 2.11% to 58,711.11. China's CSI 300 rose more than 4% after a rare intraday state media readout said policymakers would do more to stop the market's slide, and its chip index had its biggest one day gain on record, about 17% (CNBC; Wind). Japan's Kioxia rose nearly 9% on reports of a partnership with Nvidia (Saxo). At about 9am ET, S&P 500 futures were up 1.7% and Nasdaq 100 futures 2.4% (CNBC); MarketWatch had the same Nasdaq figure.
signals.so_what: The money is going back into the same AI and chip names that led the selloff. Who gets paid first: memory and chip equipment makers, where the scarce supply sits. The tariff read is the second driver: markets are treating the 14 economy proposal as a bargaining chip, which is what the Nov 26 brief expected. What would make this wrong: a hot ISM or jobs number next week that pushes January hike odds higher, or Monday giving the gains back on full volume. A rally on a half day after a holiday has a poor record as a signal on its own. No beneficiaries are listed: a price bounce does not change who gets paid.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new entries today. Volume will be light, so a cross of WM 247.90, AMGN 482.18 or any other trigger today will not reach 1.5x normal. Puts: VIX will likely drop with this rally, so premiums get thinner; no put passed the screen anyway. Long term: no change. Wait for Monday's close and volume.

signals.title: Nvidia: Blackwell chips reported at a Shanghai site tied to Megaspeed, while the stock bounces premarket
signals.since_yesterday: A Bloomberg investigation says a Blackwell rack, which may not be shipped to China, was installed at a Shanghai data center linked to Megaspeed's founder.
signals.what_happened: Bloomberg reported Friday that two Chinese firms installed Nvidia Blackwell chips, which US rules bar from China, in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the founder of Megaspeed and the woman at the center of the Nvidia controversy (Bloomberg; CNBC). Nvidia's response was not found. NVDA was still up about 2.6% at 153.19 before the open (CNBC). This comes two days after S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on watch for a cut.
signals.so_what: The question is no longer only governance. If US chips keep reaching China through third parties, Commerce can tighten rules on overseas data centers and resellers, and the Senate hearing in December gets harder. Who pays: Nvidia and any cloud that rents its chips to Chinese firms abroad. Who gets paid: Chinese chipmakers if access closes further, which fits Friday's record jump in China's chip index. This is one outlet's investigation so far; confidence is medium until Nvidia or Commerce responds.
signals.for_you: No action. NVDA has no buy point (under its falling 200 day at 202.62). No puts on NVDA: this headline risk can move it 5% to 10% in a day.

signals.title: Black Friday: online spending is up about 9%, but part of that is higher prices
signals.what_happened: Adobe counted $82.5 billion of US online spending from Nov 1 to 22, up 9.1%, with every day above $3 billion; buy now, pay later rose 6.5% to $6.1 billion (Adobe via FinanceFeeds and mlq.ai). Adobe forecasts $6.9 billion for Thanksgiving (+8.5%), $12.9 billion for Black Friday (+9.2%) and $15.1 billion for Cyber Monday (+6.2%); actual Thanksgiving numbers were not out by early Friday. Salesforce expects $84 billion of US online sales Nov 24 to 30, up 6%. Mastercard forecasts holiday retail sales up 5.5% and says about half of that growth is higher prices (mlq.ai). Adobe says visits to retail sites sent by AI assistants are up 127% (FinanceFeeds).
signals.so_what: Spending is holding up, and that supports the Fed's case to keep hiking. If half the growth is price, real volume is up only about 3%, so retailers with pricing power do best. Who gets paid: the biggest online sellers and payment rails. Watch buy now, pay later growth: it means some shoppers are stretching. What would make this wrong: Adobe's actual Black Friday total coming in well under $12.9 billion.
signals.for_you: No action. No retail name is a swing setup. HD and MCD sit near their range highs (363.65 and 286.66), but a range break still needs a full session close on 1.5x volume.

signals.title: Oil near $97 on new Iran tension, with OPEC meeting Sunday
signals.what_happened: Kuwait's army said Thursday that two Italian nationals were killed in alleged Iranian attacks, which Tehran denied, and Israel said it was ready to strike Iran even without the US. Trump said victory was at hand but Iran still had every chance to make a deal. Early Friday Brent was about $96.51 and US crude rose 2.97% to $85.75 from Wednesday (CNBC); Saxo had Brent over $97. OPEC and its monitoring committee meet Sunday Nov 29 (Forex Factory).
signals.so_what: Oil at these levels feeds straight into the inflation numbers the Fed is watching, so it adds to hike risk. Who pays: airlines and shippers. Who gets paid: producers. Sunday's OPEC meeting can move oil before Monday's open.
signals.for_you: Long term: DAL is on the long term scan buy list at its 82.60 point, and fuel is its biggest cost. Keep any DAL buy small and wait past Sunday's meeting. CVX has a ready pullback and oil helps it, but no swing setup.

signals.title: US stocks go to 23 hour trading on Sunday Dec 6
signals.what_happened: Nasdaq says the industry move to a 23 hour, five day trading week is expected on Sunday Dec 6, 2026, pending SIP readiness and SEC rule changes; its new overnight session runs 9:00pm to 3:55am ET (Nasdaq). NYSE Arca is adding an overnight session from 9:00pm to 4:00am ET with no opening auction (NYSE).
signals.so_what: Prices will move overnight on news from Asia and Europe, on thin volume. Daily bars and the 1.5x volume rule still come from the regular session, but a TradingView alert can fire on an overnight print that the regular session never confirms.
signals.for_you: Swing: from Dec 7, a phone alert at 2am ET is a reason to look at the open, not a trigger. The rule stays a regular session close over the pivot on 1.5x the 50 day volume.

signals.title: The Nov 26 brief, graded where something new happened
signals.what_happened: No US session since the brief, so only overseas moves can grade it. (1) 'The real aim is leverage before late January': supported so far. Europe rose 1.8% Thursday, with autos among the leaders, on the view that the tariffs were less severe than feared (Saxo). (2) TM, HMC and STLA as hurt: not supported yet. European autos rose Thursday and the Nikkei rose 2.11% Friday; US prices for these names will not show until today's session. (3) NVDA as hurt: up 2.6% premarket, but too early to grade. (4) 'No move this week can confirm on volume': still holds.
signals.so_what: The proposals hurt the exporters' stocks for one morning, then the market priced in deals. The hurt list was right about who pays if the tariffs happen, and early about the price move.
signals.for_you: No action. Keep the no puts on autos rule until the Jan 25 hearings; one up day does not remove the risk.

signals.title: Data check: a holiday shows up as 'Stale prices'
signals.what_happened: meta.json says the Nov 26 session 'should be in', but Nov 26 was Thanksgiving. The check in site_data.py does not know market holidays. The routine says to trigger a refresh on that warning; it was not run today because there was no session to fetch.
signals.so_what: A warning that fires on every holiday teaches us to ignore it, and then it will be missed on a day it matters. The fix is a US market holiday list in the check, with a test for Thanksgiving and the day after Christmas.
signals.for_you: No action. All levels in this brief are Wednesday Nov 25 closes unless marked premarket.

cycle.quadrant_why: No new US data since core PCE at 3.3% and Q3 GDP at 4.3% (BEA). Oil near $97 adds to inflation pressure. Overseas, inflation is cooling: Spain fell to 4.1% and France to 2.9% in November (CNBC). The All Weather model's season is not changed.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late. A Dec 9 hike was about 98% priced on Wednesday, and a strong holiday season makes it harder for the Fed to pause.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. China is again promising to prop up its stock market, a sign of an economy leaning on policy support.
cycle.big_cycle: External order: tariffs as leverage, with deals priced in. Technology: AI chips are now a security issue, with US chips reported inside China despite the rules. Internal order: the President called for a probe of the GDP revision (CNBC).
tailwinds: Europe and Asia rallied hard on Thursday and Friday (Saxo; CNBC).
Markets treat the tariff proposals as bargaining.
headwinds: A December hike close to certain.

history.what: The Fed hiked four times into a strong economy. The S&P 500 fell 19.8% from Sept 20 to Dec 24, 2018, just short of a bear market, and the Fed then paused in January 2019.
history.lesson: Hikes into strength can knock stocks down hard without a recession. The bottom came when the Fed signaled it would stop, not when the data turned.

cycle.differences: In 2018 inflation was close to the Fed's goal, so it could pause quickly. Today core PCE is 3.3% and rising, so a fast pause is less likely. Some investors told 3Fourteen Research they fear a replay of 2018 (CNBC).
cycle.for_you: Swing: wait for a full session close with volume; Monday or later. Puts: premiums may shrink as fear eases. Long term: small pieces only, and watch oil for DAL.
